target: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Observability and Monitoring Design v4.docx

fixes.old: No per-service dashboard shows a case identifier, account number, name or national ID. A panel that needs to follow one case uses the Temporal workflow ID, and the payload stays encrypted (Architecture v5 slide 35; E2-038).
fixes.new: Each of the 19 services publishes one alert and dashboard page. The page carries latency, error rate, consumer lag, dead-letter count and outbox age for that service, and the service's run book page cites it. Latency and error rate use the Latency and Error rate alerts of section 2.1. Dead-letter count and outbox age use the Exception queue growing alert (more than 50 items or older than one day). A consumer lag threshold, an SLO and an error budget: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0311).

fixes.old: The four paragraphs above keep their ownership. The realignment adds the per-service split: because an alert now names a service, its run book does too, and the service that owns the signal is the owner of the run book. The DevOps team is the suggested owner of that work, and any team may pick up the story (Rules v1 R5.3).
fixes.new: The run book page of each service cites that service's alert and dashboard page (section 3.1).

fixes.old: An alert names one service and one signal, so the same threshold crossing in two services opens two incidents, one per service, and never one incident for the Workbench.
fixes.new: Dead-letter events: the platform administrator receives the alert of the .dlt topic and runs the replay tool; the owning service fixes the cause (Architecture v5 slide 22).

disposition.note: Per-service alert and dashboard page and run book citation added; consumer lag threshold left unspecified. Anchors come from the B-TECH-09 v4 markdown; docview was not run.
Replay role and platform/service split recorded in section 2.2. Anchor comes from the B-TECH-09 v4 markdown; the docx itself was not read.
